name: rowVars
title: Variance estimates for each row in a matrix

origin.description: Variance estimates for each row (column) in a matrix.
origin.usage:
rowVars(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, refine = TRUE,
  center = NULL, dim. = dim(x), ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: refine
arguments.text: If TRUE, center is NULL, and x is numeric, extra effort is used to calculate the average with greater numerical precision.

arguments.name: center
arguments.text: Optional vector of length N. Pre-specified row means. NULL estimates them internally. A length-1 value is an error.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when not a matrix. The argument is named with a period so it does not clash with dim.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: With center NULL, the installed C routine returns the unbiased sample variance, sum((x - mean)^2) / (n - 1). For numeric x and refine TRUE it first corrects the mean by the mean of the residuals. Fewer than two values, or any missing value when na.rm is FALSE, is NA. A supplied center uses n/(n-1) * mean((x - center)^2). The other formula, mean(x^2) - center^2, is compared on the first call and then every 50.
origin.value: A numeric vector of length N.

translation.description: Variance estimates for each row in a matrix.
translation.usage:
rowVars(x, rows=None, cols=None, na_rm=False, refine=True,
        center=None, dim=None, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d array whose axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A 1-d vector is accepted when dim is set; it is filled column-major, as R stores a matrix. Integer values use the integer path, with R's integer NA equal to -2147483648. Floating values are computed as float64. Logical input is rejected.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. Zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and logical values are recycled.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column. The scan walks the selected columns in this order.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, NaN values are excluded. This is na.rm. False stores R's NA when any value is missing. Double NA is NaN.

arguments.name: refine
arguments.text: If True, center is omitted, and x is floating point, a second pass adds the mean of the residuals before the squared deviations. Integer arrays do not use that pass.

arguments.name: center
arguments.text: Optional float vector of length N, the pre-specified row means. None estimates them with the C routine. A length-1 value is an error. On the first call, and then every 50, a center that is not the sample mean raises the installed formula error.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the number of rows and columns. This is dim. in R. None uses the shape of a 2-d x. A 1-d x is filled in column-major order.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument useNames. It must be TRUE or FALSE. The result is a plain float64 vector, with no names attached.

translation.details: The scan lives in the Rust crate rowvars, ported from matrixStats src/rowVars.c. The result is sum((x - mean)^2) / (n - 1). refine matches the residual correction in that C code. A supplied center follows R/rowVars.R: n/(n-1) * mean((x - center)^2), with infinite centers written onto the row before the mean. R's NA is the NaN whose bits are 0x7ff00000000007a2.
translation.value: A float64 vector of length equal to the number of selected rows.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowvars import rowVars

x = np.arange(1, 13).reshape((4, 3), order="F")
rowVars(x)
